Search exact and synonymous wording, identify the paper(s), and extract follow-up duration, implant model/material/surface, fixation method, patient cohort, and outcomes. Distinguish true 10-year results from shorter follow-up or different stem designs.'}

## Conclusion

**Yes.** A published clinical report specifically describes a 10-year result for a **cemented, fine-grit-blasted titanium–aluminum–vanadium hip stem/shaft**.

### Matching paper

**PMID:** 10730364  
**Title:** *[10 year results with a cemented fine-grit-blasted titanium-aluminum-vanadium hip endoprosthesis shaft]*  
**Journal/year:** *Zeitschrift für Orthopädie und ihre Grenzgebiete*, 2000

The title and abstract use “shaft” and “stem” interchangeably. The abstract contains a likely translation/OCR variant, “mild grid blasted,” but the title specifies **fine-grit-blasted**.

| Item | Reported information |
|---|---|
| Follow-up | Kaplan–Meier result reported at **10 years**; mean clinical/radiographic follow-up was **11 years 4 months** |
| Implant | Cemented titanium–aluminum–vanadium femoral stem/shaft |
| Material | Titanium–aluminum–vanadium; the abstract does not explicitly print the designation **Ti-6Al-4V**, although that is consistent with the wording in the title/query |
| Surface | Fine-grit-blasted surface |
| Fixation | **Cemented** femoral component |
| Arthroplasty | Total hip arthroplasty |
| Implant model | **Not identified in the accessible abstract**; no commercial model should be inferred |
| Cohort | 71 men, mean age 56.1 years; 130 women, mean age 59.3 years. Only **35% of all patients** could be reexamined both clinically and radiographically |
| Functional outcome | Mean Merle d’Aubigné score increased from **10.5 to 16.0** |
| Radiographic outcome | Gruen-zone radiolucent lines occurred in **1%–22%**, varying by zone and femoral-component size |
| Revision outcome | **18 femoral-component reoperations**, reported as 2.9% |
| Survivorship | **95.4% femoral-component survival at 10 years** by Kaplan–Meier analysis |

### Interpretation and limitations

This is a **true 10-year clinical result**, not merely a study with less than 10 years of follow-up: the paper explicitly reports 10-year survivorship, with an average follow-up exceeding 11 years.

However, the accessible abstract does **not** establish:

- the commercial stem model;
- the exact alloy designation as Ti-6Al-4V;
- stem geometry;
- cement brand or detailed cementing technique;
- the precise denominator for the 2.9% reoperation rate;
- whether the 201 sex/age observations represent the entire treated cohort or the reexamined subgroup.

### Distinction from nonmatching studies

The synonym searches retrieved other titanium or grit-blasted stems, but these were not equivalent evidence. Examples included **cementless** stems and different designs with approximately five- or seven-year follow-up. They should not be counted as 10-year results for the cemented fine-grit-blasted Ti–Al–V shaft.

**Bottom line:** PMID **10730364** is the directly matching published report and supports a 10-year femoral-component survivorship of **95.4%**, with mean follow-up of **11 years 4 months**.
